scope: M4 decision core (SAN single-loss and per-game-day thresholds, temporary/indefinite/permanent insanity state, Luck spend eligibility and post-adjustment band, Luck recovery, skill-growth tick and settlement) plus its native integration in module/apps/sanity.mjs, module/apps/luck.mjs, module/apps/charDev.mjs, module/apps/check.mjs and module/apps/worldTime.mjs. The core itself stays pure; the app layer owns actor writes, ActiveEffects, dice and chat cards.

integration.writePolicy: All SAN settlements and keeper actions run on game.users.activeGM. A non-writer rewrites the card loss to a socket request; the writer serializes the read-modify-write and applies it once. Luck spends/spends are serialized on the active GM and also gated by the ruleset at settlement, not only in the UI.
integration.tests: tools/tests/coc-sanity-regressions.mjs (45 pure checks) and tools/tests/rules-regressions.mjs (161 checks in the headless compat mirror; 47 of them M4).

licenseBoundary.facts: Only numeric values, dice formulas, thresholds, field semantics and URLs are recorded. All prose, tag names and state names in module/rules/coc-sanity.mjs were written for this project.
excluded: No Call of Cthulhu 7e Foundry VTT system source, template, YAML, data or implementation was read or referenced.
No other GPL system implementation was used.
No official PDF, text block, table layout, image, font, logo or trade dress is committed.
The ten bout-of-madness entries are stored as 1..10 index plus a short project-authored id and zh label; the official description sentences are not reproduced.
No Pulp Cthulhu talent or Pulp-only Luck spend is enabled; Pulp-only ids are listed so an integration cannot enable them by accident.

sources.title: Official Call of Cthulhu 7e Quick-Start Rules
usedFor: SAN roll is 1D100 against current SAN; loss written as pass/fail pair
A loss of 5 or more from a single SAN roll requires a 1D100 roll against INT
INT result equal to or less than INT means temporarily insane for 1D10 hours
Failed INT roll means the investigator stays sane for now
A bout of madness is rolled on 1D10 and played round by round
Once 1D10 hours pass the investigator is sane again; delusions stop, phobias/manias/backstory changes remain
Characteristics are percentile values (STR 60 means 60%) and an uncovered test uses the characteristic like a skill
Successful skill use earns one check; end-of-scenario 1D100 over the skill value adds 1D10
sources.note: Parsed for facts only; no text block is stored.

sources.title: Official wiki: Sanity
usedFor: 5 or more points lost from a single SAN roll = major emotional trauma, then 1D100 <= INT
Success means temporary insanity for 1D10 hours; failure means the mind closes and the investigator remains sane
Temporarily insane investigators suffer a bout of madness resolved with 1D10
Bouts of madness table has exactly ten entries at index 1..10, each lasting 1D10 rounds; entries 9 and 10 add a phobia and a mania
Delusions end with the 1D10 hour period; phobias, manias and altered backstory remain
sources.note: The page documents temporary insanity only; it carries no indefinite-insanity rule.

sources.title: Official wiki: The Game System
usedFor: On a successful skill roll put a check next to that skill; one check per skill at a time
Regular success = roll <= value, Hard = roll <= half, Extreme = roll <= one fifth
Pushed rolls exist and cannot be combined with Luck spending in the standard procedure
Luck roll succeeds on roll <= current Luck

sources.title: Official wiki: Rewards of Success
usedFor: Only checked skills (used and rolled successfully) are rolled for improvement
Improvement roll is 1D100 strictly over the current value
A successful improvement adds 1D10 to the skill value
No INT bonus and no fixed improvement tier are part of the check

sources.title: Official wiki: Step Two - Secondary Attributes
usedFor: SAN begins equal to POW and is used as a percentile roll
Luck is 3D6 x 5 and a Luck roll succeeds on roll <= current Luck
Luck therefore has no printed ceiling other than the 99 used below (see coc-roll20-using-luck)

sources.title: Official free scenario: The Lightless Beacon (Introducing Spending Luck)
usedFor: Luck may adjust a skill roll on a 1-for-1 basis, and may raise the degree of success
Luck may NOT be spent to adjust a Sanity roll
Luck may NOT be spent on rolls that determine how much Sanity is lost
Luck may NOT be spent to adjust a pushed roll or a fumbled roll
Luck may NOT be spent on weapon malfunction outcomes, damage rolls or Luck rolls
The only limit on a spend is the Luck currently remaining; spent Luck is gone for later Luck rolls
Official free indefinite-insanity wording: losing one fifth or more of STARTING Sanity cumulatively as the scenario proceeds
Pre-generated thresholds corroborate the one-fifth-of-starting figure: SAN 50 -> 10+, SAN 65 -> 13+, SAN 60 -> 12+
sources.note: Only the luck-spend prohibitions and the one-fifth arithmetic are used. The scenario's prose, investigators and handouts are not copied.

sources.title: Roll20 Compendium: Using Luck (transcription of the Keeper Rulebook procedure)
usedFor: Luck cannot be spent on Luck rolls, damage rolls, the result of a pushed roll, Sanity rolls, or skill experience checks
A critical success only arises from a natural 01; using Luck to lower a roll to 01 gives an Extreme success, not a critical
Skill experience checks are only earned for successes made without spending Luck
Luck recovery: start of session 1D100 against current Luck; higher than current adds 2D10+10, otherwise adds 1D10+5; Luck may never exceed 99 and the starting value is not a cap
Halving a failed Sanity loss by spending double the loss is listed under investigator Luck spends
sources.note: This page mixes standard investigator Luck spends with Pulp-only ones (hit-point recovery, avoiding death, staying conscious). Those Pulp entries are recorded as excluded, not implemented. Halving Sanity loss conflicts with the official free scenario's prohibition on spending Luck on Sanity-loss rolls, so the standard core keeps it disabled.

sources.title: TRPGLine system reference: Call of Cthulhu 7th (Keeper Rulebook transcription)
usedFor: Three insanity states: temporary, indefinite, permanent
Indefinite insanity on losing a fifth or more of CURRENT Sanity points in one game day
Permanent insanity when Sanity reaches 0, and the investigator ceases to be a playable character
Indefinite insanity lasts until cured or recovered; treatment is monthly private care or institutionalization
sources.note: Tertiary transcription. Recorded as the only available wording for the current-SAN basis and for permanent insanity; the recovery quantities are NOT recorded as fact.

singleLossThreshold.appliedTo: the Sanity points lost as the consequence of a single Sanity roll, after clamping to remaining SAN

intCheck.rule: 1D100 roll; result <= INT means temporarily insane, > INT means remains sane
intCheck.missingDiePolicy: pending; never treated as success or failure

temporaryInsanityDuration.note: Duration in hours is returned as data. Elapsed time is confirmed by an explicit keeper event; this module never infers expiry from a clock.

boutOfMadness.note: Only index, die type and the 9/10 phobia-mania fact are used. Entry ids and zh labels are project-authored.

temporaryInsanityEnd.rule: after 1D10 hours the investigator is sane again; delusions stop, phobias/manias/altered backstory remain
temporaryInsanityEnd.note: The core requires an explicit end reason and never reports automatic recovery from elapsed model time.

permanentInsanity.rule: Sanity reaching 0 means permanent insanity; the investigator is no longer playable
permanentInsanity.note: Corroborated only by a tertiary transcription; the number 0 is also implied by the free sources' loss arithmetic. No recovery path is implemented.

indefiniteInsanity.trigger: cumulative Sanity loss of at least one fifth of a basis value
indefiniteInsanity.window: one game day as declared by the keeper
indefiniteInsanity.conflict: The official free scenario measures one fifth of STARTING Sanity cumulatively over the scenario; the Keeper Rulebook transcription measures one fifth of CURRENT Sanity within one game day.
indefiniteInsanity.resolution: The core accepts an explicit basis (`day-start` | `starting` | `current`) and returns the basis and threshold it used. `day-start` is the default because it needs a keeper-declared snapshot and invents neither basis. Without a basis value the threshold is null and no trigger can fire.

recovery.note: Monthly private-care/institutionalization roll quantities are not recorded from any verifiable primary text. Only a keeper-review marker is returned.

gameDayAnchor.definition: explicit keeper snapshot: a caller-supplied dayId plus the SAN at day start
gameDayAnchor.reason: The pure core never reads a clock. The integration persists a world-scoped CoC world clock (brp.worldTime) and a keeper day sequence (brp.cocDaySeq), restores them on load and advances them only through keeper actions; game.time.worldTime may restart at 0, so it is mirrored rather than trusted.

luckSpendEligible.cost: 1 Luck point per 1 point of roll adjustment

luckSpendForbidden.note: The free scenario forbids pushed/fumbled rolls, weapon malfunction, damage, Sanity rolls, Sanity-loss rolls and Luck rolls. Growth checks are forbidden by the secondary source and follow from the 'successes made without spending Luck' rule.

luckCritical.rule: a critical is only a natural 01; spending Luck to reach 01 yields an Extreme success
luckCritical.note: Implemented as a hard downgrade in applyLuckSpend; the adjusted result is always lower than or equal to the natural one because spends are positive.

luckRecovery.rule: session start 1D100 against current Luck; roll > current adds 2D10+10, roll <= current adds 1D10+5; cap 99
luckRecovery.note: Both branches implemented with injected D10 values and an explicit 99 cap. The starting Luck value is not treated as a cap. Because the only source is secondary, the result is tagged with that grade so the integration can gate or label it.

luckSanLossHalving.rule: spend twice the Sanity loss to halve it
luckSanLossHalving.note: The secondary compendium lists it as an investigator Luck spend, while the official free scenario forbids spending Luck on rolls that determine how much Sanity is lost. Until a primary ruling is available the standard core keeps it disabled and returns `pulp-only`/disabled ids rather than a number.

growthTick.rule: tick only after a successful skill use, not when the success came from spending Luck, and not for noXP skills
growthTick.note: The 'no Luck' half is secondary; the 'only successful use' half is primary. NPC actors and non-skill rolls never tick.

growthSettlement.rule: 1D100 strictly over the current value adds 1D10; equal or lower adds nothing
growthSettlement.note: No INT bonus, no fixed tier, no cap; the module returns the injected D10 and the new value.

items: Indefinite insanity basis and window: official free wording (one fifth of starting SAN over the scenario) and the Keeper Rulebook transcription (one fifth of current SAN in one game day) disagree.
Indefinite insanity recovery quantities and cadence (private care vs institutionalization rolls).
Whether spending double the Sanity loss to halve it is a standard or Pulp-era option; the free scenario forbids Luck on Sanity-loss rolls.
The 'game day' calendar definition: no in-world calendar exists in the runtime.
Permanent insanity's exact book wording; only a tertiary transcription was reachable.
Whether the 96-100 fumble band for skills below 50 belongs to the free rules text; it is inherited from the M1 band and reused here unchanged.

notImplemented: Any third-party system's sanity automation or code.
Pulp talents: avoiding death, hit-point recovery, staying conscious, and any other Pulp-only Luck spend.
Automatic recovery of any insanity state from elapsed model time.
Writing actor data, creating ActiveEffects, rolling dice, or sending chat cards from this module.
